To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new distributed fair queueing algorithm, maximize-local-minimum (MLM), for wireless ad hoc networks that achieves fairness and spatial channel reuse, and that we extend MLM to enhanced MLM (EMLM) to further improve spatial reuse.
we propose an efficient and scalable fair queueing scheme for wireless ad hoc networks that is self-coordinating and localized, and achieves global fairness in a distributed fashion.

(i) the spatial locality of the wireless channel complicates the fairness definition; (ii) self-coordinating fair scheduling algorithms can provide global fairness in wireless ad hoc network; (iii) the self-coordination mechanism should be localized to reduce the overhead and improve scalability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation of a self-coordinating distributed fair queueing algorithm for multihop wireless ad hoc networks, which is the first work in this direction to the best of our knowledge.
the following questions: (1) What is fair queueing for wireless ad hoc networks?
the design, implementation, and analysis of fair queueing algorithms in wireless ad hoc and sensor networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a thorough analysis and design of fair queueing in multihop wireless networks.
the paper presents a novel distributed packet scheduler that provides fair bandwidth allocation and high spatial channel reuse in wireless ad hoc and sensor networks.
our proposed self-coordinating fair queueing algorithms achieve global fairness in a distributed manner and are efficient in terms of spatial reuse of the shared wireless channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an effective and efficient localized design that can be easily implemented in a distributed fashion.
a distributed fair queueing algorithm for ad hoc networks can be designed to achieve global fairness by self-coordinating local schedulers.
a localized fair queueing algorithm, which is oblivious to the global network state, can achieve global fair queueing in the presence of spatial locality and channel contention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a localized design is capable of achieving the global fairness requirement in a wireless ad hoc network.
a self-coordinating design is an effective approach to achieve global fairness in a distributed ad hoc network.
the fairness notion in a multihopping wireless ad hoc network should be formulated as maximizing the minimum local throughput.
